pack.name: pack
pack.description: Read the codebase. One call can search with surrounding lines, read whole files or line ranges, get a symbol's full source, list a file's outline, or show git status. Put several items in one call to get everything in one round trip. Output is size-capped and secrets are redacted. Read-only.

items.description: What to fetch, in order. Each item has an op.

pattern.description: search: the text or regex to find.

literal.description: search: treat pattern as plain text, not a regex.

globs.description: search: only these files, gitignore-style (prefix ! to exclude).

context.description: search: lines of context around each match (default 2).

max_matches.description: search: stop after this many matching lines (default 200).

path.description: read: the file. symbol: limit to this file or directory.

ranges.description: read: [[first, last], ...] 1-based, inclusive. Omit for the whole file.

lang.description: symbol: limit to a language (py, rs, ts, go, ...).

paths.description: outline: files or directories. Omit for the whole project.

max_bytes.description: Total size cap for the answer. Lower it for a quick look; the plugin's limit still applies.

exec.name: exec
exec.description: Run Python in a persistent sandboxed kernel; returns when the cell ends. Top-level await works, variables persist between calls, the last expression is the result. In code: `await harness.tool(name, **args)` calls any tool; `await harness.parallel([(name, args), ...], limit=N)` runs several at once (a failed call leaves its error in its slot); `await harness.sh([argv], timeout)` runs a command; `await harness.leave_blank(question, options)` asks the owner without stopping. The workspace is read-only (only ship changes files); `harness.scratch` is writable; no network unless allowed. Long output is saved to a file. A cell that never yields is killed and its variables are lost.

code.description: The Python source of one cell.

timeout_ms.description: How long the cell may run, in milliseconds. A cell that runs longer is cancelled and the kernel keeps its variables.

ship.name: ship
ship.description: Change files. This is the only way to write the workspace. Send all the edits of one change together. Every edit is checked before anything is written (a miss writes nothing and shows the closest match); then the project's gate runs. If the gate fails, every file is put back exactly and you get the failing output. Paths are relative to the project; protected files (tests, secrets, keys, .git) cannot be changed.

edits.description: The edits, applied in order; each sees the result of the ones before it.

op.description: replace: swap old for new once (or every occurrence with replace_all). create: write a whole new file. delete: remove a file. diff: apply a unified diff.

path.description: The file. Optional for a diff that names its files.

old.description: replace: the exact existing text. It must occur exactly once unless replace_all is set.

new.description: replace: the replacement text (may be empty).

overwrite.description: create: allow replacing an existing file.

dispatch.name: dispatch
dispatch.description: Hand one task to the governed model cascade. Write a brief that starts with `scope:` (the project-relative paths or globs the worker may change) and `goal:`, then the approach. The system picks the model, runs a worker on the cheapest tier, and climbs to a stronger one only when the project's gate blocks; you never choose a model. Returns at once; the outcome (passed at some tier, or failed after the last tier) arrives later as a message. One task at a time.

brief.description: The brief: lines `scope: <paths or globs>` and `goal: <one or two sentences>`, then the files and functions to change, the approach and edge cases, in about 250 words. No test line: the gate runs the project's own command.
